text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- Two parties in Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), Porozumienie Centrum (PC) and the Zjednoczenie Chrescijansko Narodowe (ZChN) Christian national union have called for voting against the recently-passed constitution in a referendum on May 25. AWS and the right-wing Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) should form a common list of candidates before the elections to get 40 percent of the vote and a parliamentary majority, PC leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski said.

- Poland's inflation will go below 17 percent this month and drop to around 16 percent in May this year, National Bank of Poland (NBP) president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said. The central bank is not planning to cut interest rates in the next two or three months, she said at a meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in London.
- The Polish Liquid Gas Chamber (PIPG) will introduce protective removable seals on gas bottles which will carry information on the bottler and distributor, the PIPG said.

- Poland's food prices inched up by 0.5 percent in the last 10 days of March compared with the same period the month before, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. Vegetable and fruit prices went up by 2.2 percent and dairy products by 1.5 percent while meat prices declined by 0.3 percent.
- Holland's Gasunie aims to sign a contract on gas deliveries to Poland with the PGNiG gas mining and distribution firm this year, Gasunie's president said.

- The Polspan-Krosnopan chipboard maker got the go-ahead to develop a chipboard plant in the Mielec special Economic Zone (SEZ) in southeastern Poland employing up to 500 workers. The project involves investment of 160 million zlotys.

- Poland's electrical energy sector will have to invest between $18 billion and $30 billion in facility development in coming years to compete successfully with EU energy suppliers, some experts said.
- Poland's juice and drinks production grew by 48 percent in 1996, a survey by the Indicator market research firm said.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will invest $100 million in various development schemes in Poland this year, despite proposals to redeploy the bank's financial assistance eastward to ex-Soviet countries.

- Poland's banking sector netted 4.6 billion zlotys last year, which showed a 40 percent growth compared with the year before. Results of the insurance sector improved as well, though only 23 out of 42 surveyed companies made net profits, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
